We study a two-state inelastic dark-matter model in which $χ_1$ and $χ_2$ couple off-diagonally to an axion-like particle (ALP) that also couples to gluons and photons. Unlike treatments that assume only one dark-matter state is present today, we track the cosmological evolution of both states. The excited state $χ_2$ is sufficiently long-lived to survive to the present, with its relic fraction determined by the dark-sector conversion process $χ_2χ_2\leftrightarrowχ_1χ_1$. We find that this fraction depends strongly on the Lorentz structure of the DM--ALP interaction. Scalar transition couplings lead to nonperturbative conversion rates with a pronounced resonant structure, yielding a final excited-state fraction that varies nonmonotonically with the mediator mass, from $f_2\sim10^{-4}$ to approximately $1/2$ over the parameter range studied. The relative importance of endothermic and exothermic scattering is therefore parameter dependent. By contrast, pseudoscalar transition couplings preserve $f_2\simeq1/2$, yielding recoil spectra dominated by exothermic $χ_2 N\toχ_1 N$ down-scattering for the benchmarks considered. Benchmark spectra in all four scenarios can peak near the observed recoil energy of $250\,\mathrm{keV}$. Our results demonstrate that the dominant direction of inelastic scattering in direct detection can be dynamically selected by the early-Universe evolution of the dark sector. With additional data, annual modulation measurements could distinguish these scenarios. We further show that the ALP portal can be directly probed at colliders.

papers.title: Constraints on Complex Electroweak WIMPs from Solar Capture
papers.abstract: One of the most convincing realizations of particle dark matter is provided by models based on electroweak multiplets. The lightest neutral state of such a multiplet can be a stable Majorana fermion or a real scalar, and its phenomenology is governed by two parameters: the dark matter mass and the mass splitting $\{m_χ,δ\}$. The sub-MeV range for $δ$ is particularly important as it allows for a large inelastic scattering cross section. In this paper, we analyze solar capture, energy loss, and annihilation of scalar and fermionic electroweak multiplet dark matter, generalizing earlier results for the Higgsino to other representations. We find that, while the case of a doublet is somewhat special, higher representations behave in a self-similar way. For the higher multiplets, IceCube results constrain the splitting to $δ\gtrsim 350$ keV for all dark matter masses up to $100$ TeV. Assuming thermal freeze-out and a Standard Halo Model velocity distribution, this rules out most models of electroweak dark matter as a possible origin of the single high-recoil event reported by the LZ collaboration. We also show that a high-velocity tail in the dark matter distribution, such as that induced by the Large Magellanic Cloud, raises the splitting preferred by the LZ event above the solar bounds for many of the multiplets.

papers.title: Two-loop $gg\to AA$ amplitudes near threshold and the double parton scattering singularity
papers.abstract: The two-loop amplitudes for pseudoscalar pair production in gluon fusion, $gg\to AA$, with each pseudoscalar emitted from its own effective gluon vertex, are known in closed form, but large cancellations near threshold obscure their analytic structure. We expand the IR-finite amplitudes in the pseudoscalar velocity $β_A$ through $β_A^6$ at fixed scattering angle. All inverse powers of $β_A$ and the odd powers through $β_A^5$ cancel, and at leading power the angular dependence enters only through $\ln(2p_T/m_A)$. We identify this logarithm with the double parton scattering (DPS) singularity: with the overall constant fixed at threshold, the factorisation formula of Gaunt and Stirling reproduces the velocity dependence of its one-loop coefficient in the forward limit exactly, and a one-loop $gg\to HH$ analysis confirms the corresponding CP-even helicity sum. At two loops the equal-helicity amplitude grows as $\ln^3(2p_T/m_A)$, and the ratio of its leading two- and one-loop logarithms agrees with that in planar $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory, while the opposite-helicity amplitude, which has no one-loop DPS logarithm, grows as $\ln^2(2p_T/m_A)$. In the finite virtual correction, relative to the squared tree amplitude, the highest logarithm at order $α_s^2$ is $-\tfrac{7}{64}α_s^2N_c^2\ln^2(2p_T/m_A)$. For $β_A\leq0.2$ the series reproduce the unexpanded amplitudes with relative errors of at most $6.77\times10^{-5}$ at the tested points; they provide this two-loop contribution to the hard function for soft-gluon resummation of the pair invariant-mass distribution near $m_{AA}=2m_A$ and are released with code for their numerical evaluation.

papers.title: Exothermic Dark Matter with a Dark Higgs: The LZ 248 keV Event and the Galactic Center Excess
papers.abstract: LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) reported a $248~\mathrm{keV}$ nuclear-recoil candidate. Exothermic dark matter can explain it in a dark $U(1)$ model whose dark Higgs generates the dark photon mass and the mass splitting. Since the dark photon mass sets both the excited-state fraction and the scattering rate, two dark photon masses explain the event, near $1$ and $25~\mathrm{GeV}$ for kinetic mixing $ε=10^{-4}$. Cosmic microwave background limits exclude most of the lighter branch. On the heavier branch, the southern-sky Galactic Center $γ$-ray excess complements the LZ event by selecting a dark matter mass of $40$-$44~\mathrm{GeV}$, and its fit favors a dark Higgs boson near the dark photon mass.

papers.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
papers.abstract: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.

papers.title: SecRed: A program for sector-wise IBP reduction of Feynman integrals
papers.abstract: SecRed is a C++ program for the reduction of multi-loop Feynman integrals with integration-by-parts (IBP) identities. It reduces an integral family sector by sector for memory control and parallelism, and adds algorithms designed for that setting: an adaptive seed box with a corner cut, an optional seed truncation, a subsector level filter, and symmetry relations expanded only from the master integrals of a sector. A global stage assembles the retained equations and performs the finite-field reconstruction of the coefficients using FiniteFlow or FireFly, repeating the elimination over a sequence of primes. On the elimination side, a coefficient-free plan records the elimination order once and is replayed at each prime, so that only the arithmetic is repeated, and a head score orders the equations to reduce fill-in during the elimination. The program is demonstrated on a two-loop five-point non-planar family and on a four-loop cut family, where assembling the global equation system as a whole would exceed the memory of a single node.

papers.title: Next-to-leading order QCD corrections to fully charm tetraquark radiative decays
papers.abstract: We present the first complete next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD calculation of the fully charm tetraquark radiative decays $T_{4c}(0^{++},2^{++})\toγJ/ψ$ and $T_{4c}(1^{+-})\toγη_c$ at leading order in the relative velocity. The NLO widths are $2.3$--$3.1$ times the leading-order (LO) widths for the long-distance matrix element (LDME) inputs considered here, with $m_c=1.5$ GeV and $μ_R=2m_c$. In the scalar channel, the NLO corrections change the relative contributions of the two color-spin components and their interference. For the tensor channel, the longitudinal fraction $f_L$ of the daughter $J/ψ$ changes from $0.11$ at LO to $0.18$ at strictly expanded NLO, with sensitivity to higher-order corrections. These NLO results provide valuable theoretical input for searches for states predicted to lie near their respective lowest dicharmonium thresholds and for probing the spin and short-distance structure of tetraquark candidates.

papers.title: Probing soft signals of gravitational-wave memory with space-based interferometers
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave displacement memory is a remarkable, ubiquitous prediction of general relativity that has not yet been detected. Unlike the oscillatory components of gravitational waveforms, displacement memory is associated with soft gravitons and provides the leading low-frequency observable of its parent event. Analogous soft signals may also be associated with velocity and integrated-displacement memory. The simple, universal spectral shapes of soft waveforms provide effective templates for matched filtering and parameter estimation. In this paper, we investigate the detection prospects for such soft memory signals with future space-based laser interferometers. As realistic examples, we examine the infrared spectral features of gravitational waves from moderately relativistic nonspinning compact binary scattering and comparable-mass quasicircular, nonprecessing black hole mergers. In both cases, the low-frequency spectrum can be described by a soft displacement-memory waveform with finite-frequency corrections. Using the adopted instrumental-noise models, simulated Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses show that a single LISA-like detector can constrain the memory amplitude and arrival time for signals with matched-filter signal-to-noise ratios of order 10. Big Bang Observer (BBO) Stage 1 could measure null displacement memory from sufficiently loud stellar-mass compact binary mergers. We also evaluate the detectability of an idealized stochastic background of soft displacement-memory signals. These results establish gravitational-wave bursts with memory as concrete targets for space-based interferometers.

papers.title: How many degrees of freedom describe a quantum N-particle state?
papers.abstract: In Newtonian spacetime, the canonical description of a classical $N$-particle system requires $3N$ degrees of freedom. Not all of these are physical, however, since the conservation of the net momentum implies that only $3(N-1)$ accelerations are independent. Hence, three constraints can be used to eliminate the unphysical centre-of-mass variables, at the level of the Lagrangian, leaving only the subset of observable displacements and momenta, which are relational. Imposing the constraints does not change the dynamics of these variables, at the classical level, and is analogous to a gauge-fixing procedure, which removes redundancy in the description of the system. In classical physics, therefore, the number of physical degrees of freedom equals the number of independent relational degrees of freedom. Here, we show that this is not the case in quantum mechanics. While an operator-analogue of the classical net momentum exists, it cannot be used to impose constraints that restrict the degrees of freedom in the theory, without a loss of physical information. This means that all $3N$ canonical degrees of freedom are physical, even though only $3(N-1)$ of them are relational. We explore the physical consequences of the non-relational variables and show that they give rise to generalised uncertainty relations (GURs), for the relational quantities that define the quantum reference frame (QRF). Hence, it is shown that the non-relational degrees of freedom refer to the frame itself and that the non-Heisenberg terms in the GURs define its Galilean-invariant spreads, in both real space and momentum space. The implications of this result for recent work on relational models, including the ``perspective neutral'' framework for QRFs, are discussed. Its implications for the wider relational program, and, in particular, the relevance of the latter to quantum gravity research, are also critically assessed

papers.title: High Precision Fundamental Physics Experiments at JLab with Spin-transparent Storage Rings of Low-energy Polarized Electron Beams
papers.abstract: A breakthrough in fundamental physics experiments measuring particle spin precession may happen if spin-transparent storage rings become adopted tools for such experiments. We present a new design of highly specialized table-sized storage rings, which use low-energy polarized electron beams and Mott polarimetry. Based on the spin transparency ansatz, the spin precession stemming from the magnetic dipole moment is canceled at any beam energy after an electron's turn along the periodic orbit in the ring. Meanwhile, a spin precession induced by the fundamental physics of interest, e.g., the electron's permanent electric dipole moment (EDM) and/or ultralight-dark-matter-mediated forces such as axions, will accumulate. However, capitalizing on such types of rings is not only desirable for measurements of EDMs and axion searches relevant to $CP$ violation and matter-antimatter asymmetry in the Universe, but may also find very promising applications in quantum computing.

papers.title: Long-term 3+1 simulations of primordial black hole formation during radiation domination
papers.abstract: We develop an efficient three-dimensional numerical-relativity framework for primordial black-hole (PBH) formation from superhorizon curvature perturbations in a radiation-dominated Universe. We implement flux-conservative relativistic hydrodynamics in the adaptive-mesh-refinement code GRChombo and introduce a cosmologically scaled Gamma-driver that allows the cosmic-time step to grow in proportion to the scale factor. For a representative long-term simulation, the scaled driver preserves the apparent-horizon mass evolution and constraint behavior while reducing the number of coarse-level advances by a factor of approximately $94$ relative to the standard driver. We also construct a conformal-time version of the moving-puncture gauge as a consistency check. Applying the framework to a spherical Gaussian curvature profile, we find a collapse threshold $μ_c \simeq 0.7958$ and approximate critical mass scaling, consistent with previous spherically symmetric results. We further fit the late-time PBH mass growth to the Zel'dovich--Novikov accretion law, demonstrating that the code can follow both near-critical collapse and long-term post-formation evolution in three dimensions. The framework provides a foundation for future studies of PBH formation beyond spherical symmetry.

papers.title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.
